en.title: Weddings and family ceremonies
en.summary: Weddings, christenings and funerals, and the words used to talk about them.

paragraphs: Family ceremonies mark important moments in life: birth, marriage and death. This lesson explains the main events and teaches the past simple for telling what happened at a ceremony.

A traditional wedding in England has a ceremony, usually in a church or a register office, and a reception afterwards. The bride often wears white, the groom is supported by a best man, and bridesmaids accompany the bride. After the ceremony there is a meal, speeches and dancing. Hana went to a wedding last weekend and tells her colleague about it.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.text: I was at a wedding last Saturday. It took place in a village church.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.text: Lovely. The bride wore white, and the groom's brother gave a funny speech.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.text: Yes, in a marquee in the garden, with food, music and a cake. We danced until midnight.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.text: Yes, the couple had made a gift list, so I bought something from it.

paragraphs: **1. The past simple narrates events in order.** Regular verbs end in -ed; many common verbs are irregular. See Introduction to Grammar: Past tenses.

paragraphs: **2. Possession with 's.** An apostrophe and s show who owns something; for a plural noun ending in s, add only the apostrophe. See Introduction to Grammar: Substantives (nouns).

items: A best man supports the groom; bridesmaids accompany the bride.
A christening is a baby's religious welcome in many Christian families.
A funeral is a ceremony to say goodbye to someone who has died.
A gift list is a list of presents the couple would like.

paragraphs: Wedding customs vary: many British couples now marry in a register office or a hotel, and in the United States a large reception is typical. In many families the guests wear formal clothes and bring a card with a gift.
